edge_strength.howComputed: no_edge when the out-of-sample baseline gate fails; otherwise clear when skill − baseline_skill ≥ EDGE_MARGIN_THRESHOLD, and marginal below it.
edge_strength.whatItMeans: How comfortably the model beat a naive baseline. Treat a high probability under 'marginal' as thin evidence, not near-certainty.

skill.howComputed: Out-of-sample directional accuracy from purged walk-forward validation — the fraction of held-out bars whose direction the model called correctly.
skill.whatItMeans: How often the model was right on data it never trained on. Compare it to the baseline, not to 50% — beating the baseline is the bar that matters.

baseline_skill.howComputed: The same out-of-sample accuracy for a naive baseline — the stronger of persistence (next = current) and majority-class — scored on the identical held-out bars.
baseline_skill.whatItMeans: The score to beat. A model only has an edge when its skill clears this; a skill of 0.55 means nothing if the baseline also scores 0.55.

prob_up.howComputed: The model's calibrated probability that the next move over the horizon is up, shown only when the horizon beat its baseline out-of-sample.
prob_up.whatItMeans: The chance of an up-move as the validated model sees it. A value near one-third is barely better than a three-way coin-flip; only a decisive value under a clear edge reads as conviction.

prob_down.howComputed: The model's calibrated probability that the next move over the horizon is down, shown only when the horizon beat its baseline out-of-sample.
prob_down.whatItMeans: The chance of a down-move as the validated model sees it. Read it beside P(up) and P(flat) — the three sum to one across the outcomes.

prob_flat.howComputed: The model's calibrated probability that price is roughly unchanged over the horizon, shown only when the horizon beat its baseline out-of-sample.
prob_flat.whatItMeans: The chance of no decisive move. A high P(flat) is the model saying 'no clear direction', which is itself information.

edge_margin.howComputed: skill − baseline_skill when both were scored, otherwise blank.
edge_margin.whatItMeans: By how much the model beat the baseline. A tiny positive margin is a marginal edge; the sign and size are what separate 'clear' from 'marginal'.

n_scored.howComputed: The number of out-of-sample bars scored across all walk-forward folds at this horizon.
n_scored.whatItMeans: How much held-out evidence the skill number rests on. A high accuracy over a handful of bars is not yet a track record.

n_splits.howComputed: The number of purged walk-forward folds the model was validated across.
n_splits.whatItMeans: How many independent out-of-sample windows the edge held up over. More folds means the result is less likely a single lucky stretch.

horizon_bars.howComputed: The forecast horizon, in bars of the result's timeframe (e.g. 21 bars on a 1d series ≈ a month ahead).
horizon_bars.whatItMeans: How far ahead this block looks. Edge at one horizon says nothing about another — each is trained and gated on its own.

beats_baseline.howComputed: True when the model's out-of-sample skill cleared the baseline gate at this horizon.
beats_baseline.whatItMeans: The go/no-go for showing probabilities. When false, no probability is shown at all — an honest 'don't know' rather than a fabricated number.

feature_set_id.howComputed: A stable hash of the ordered feature set the model was trained on (e.g. price-only v1, or a v2 tier that adds cycle and on-chain inputs).
feature_set_id.whatItMeans: Which inputs the forecast saw. A v1 id means exogenous series weren't available and the model ran on price-derived features only.

model_version.howComputed: A content hash over the training-data cutoff, feature set, and library versions — the identity of the exact trained model.
model_version.whatItMeans: Provenance for reproducibility. Two forecasts with the same model_version came from the same trained model; a change means something upstream moved.

permutation_importance.howComputed: Out-of-sample permutation importance: how much the model's validated skill drops when one feature's values are shuffled.
permutation_importance.whatItMeans: Which inputs the model leaned on — association within the validated model, not causation. Correlated inputs share the credit, so read the ranking, not the exact numbers.

conviction.howComputed: P(direction) × clamp(sharpe_mean / SHARPE_FULL_CREDIT, 0, 1) — the calibrated forecast probability of the called direction times the walk-forward edge credit (linear up to SHARPE_FULL_CREDIT, zero at or below zero Sharpe).
conviction.whatItMeans: How strongly the app backs this call. Low by construction when either the forecast edge is marginal or the backtest is thin — it is derived, never invented, and a flat call has zero.

direction.howComputed: long or short only when the forecast, at least one agreeing live signal, and a positive walk-forward edge all point the same way; otherwise flat.
direction.whatItMeans: The advisory stance. 'flat — no actionable edge' is a real answer, not a missing one: at least one leg didn't line up.

entry_zone.howComputed: A band of ±ENTRY_BAND_ATR (a quarter ATR) around the last close — chart geometry, not a prediction.
entry_zone.whatItMeans: Where the call considers an entry actionable, for your judgement. Advisory only — nothing here places an order.

stop.howComputed: Beyond the nearest opposing support/resistance level with an ATR buffer, falling back to STOP_ATR (2 ATRs) from the last close when no level sits there.
stop.whatItMeans: A suggested invalidation level derived from volatility and structure — advisory, sized to where the idea would be wrong, not a guarantee.

targets.howComputed: The nearest favouring support/resistance level, falling back to TARGET_ATR (2 ATRs) from the last close when none exists.
targets.whatItMeans: Advisory objective(s) from chart structure — where price might travel if the call works, not a promise it will.

sharpe_mean.howComputed: The mean out-of-sample Sharpe ratio across the strategy's walk-forward folds (risk-adjusted return: mean return over its standard deviation).
sharpe_mean.whatItMeans: The backtested edge, averaged over held-out windows. At or above SHARPE_FULL_CREDIT it earns full conviction credit; near zero is thin; negative blocks a directional call.

sharpe_std.howComputed: The standard deviation of the per-fold Sharpe ratios across the walk-forward folds.
sharpe_std.whatItMeans: How much the edge wobbled fold to fold. A high spread beside a decent mean means the edge is inconsistent, not dependable.

total_return_mean.howComputed: The mean of the per-fold total returns across the walk-forward folds.
total_return_mean.whatItMeans: The average out-of-sample return the strategy produced per validation window — a plain-return companion to the Sharpe.

total_return_std.howComputed: The standard deviation of the per-fold total returns.
total_return_std.whatItMeans: How variable those returns were across folds. Wide swings mean the average hides a bumpy ride.

strategy_id.howComputed: The identifier of the strategy whose live signal and walk-forward edge back this call.
strategy_id.whatItMeans: Which strategy's edge this rests on. The backtested edge only counts when this same strategy also voted the called direction live.

alignment.howComputed: The fusion gate checking that every input — snapshot, forecast, signals, backtest — shares the same symbol, timeframe, and as-of bar.
alignment.whatItMeans: A consistency guard. It always passes on a shown call, because mismatched inputs are rejected before any recommendation is formed.

conditions.howComputed: The fusion leg that records the read condition snapshot — trend, momentum, and volume stance — at the as-of bar.
conditions.whatItMeans: The market backdrop the call was formed against. It's context that always registers, not a pass/fail hurdle.

forecast.howComputed: The fusion leg gating on the calibrated forecast: probabilities must have shipped (baseline beaten) and their argmax must be directional.
forecast.whatItMeans: Whether the model's probability supports a direction. A no-edge or flat forecast fails this leg and forces a flat call.

signal.howComputed: The fusion leg gating on live strategy signals: at least one must imply the called direction, none may conflict, and it must agree with the forecast.
signal.whatItMeans: Whether a live strategy actually points the same way. Conflicting or absent signals block a directional call.

backtest.howComputed: The fusion leg gating on the walk-forward edge: a basis must exist, sharpe_mean must be positive, and it must belong to one of the agreeing strategies.
backtest.whatItMeans: Whether the direction has a real, out-of-sample track record behind it — not just a live hunch.

trend.howComputed: The snapshot's trend classification from the trailing moving-average structure and slope (e.g. up / down / sideways).
trend.whatItMeans: The prevailing direction of price. A call is easier to trust when the trend, momentum, and live signal agree.

momentum.howComputed: The snapshot's momentum classification from trailing oscillators (RSI/MACD stance) at the as-of bar.
momentum.whatItMeans: Whether the move is gaining or losing steam. Rising momentum supports continuation; fading momentum warns of stalling.

volume_stance.howComputed: The snapshot's volume classification — recent volume relative to its trailing average.
volume_stance.whatItMeans: Whether participation is confirming the move. A breakout on light volume is weaker than one on heavy volume.

ret_1.whatItMeans: The most recent bar's percentage change — the shortest-term momentum input the model sees.

ret_5.whatItMeans: Short-horizon momentum over the last five bars — smoother than the one-bar return.

rsi_14.howComputed: Wilder's 14-period Relative Strength Index, a 0–100 oscillator of average gains versus losses.
rsi_14.whatItMeans: Overbought/oversold pressure. Above ~70 is stretched high, below ~30 stretched low — a condition, not a trigger.

macd.howComputed: The MACD line: the 12-period EMA minus the 26-period EMA of close.
macd.whatItMeans: Trend-following momentum. Above zero leans bullish, below zero bearish; its slope shows momentum shifting.

macd_signal.howComputed: The 9-period EMA of the MACD line.
macd_signal.whatItMeans: A smoothed reference for the MACD line; crossings of the two are the classic momentum signal.

macd_hist.howComputed: The MACD histogram: MACD line minus its signal line.
macd_hist.whatItMeans: How fast momentum is changing. Growing bars mean momentum accelerating; shrinking bars, fading.

bb_pct_b.howComputed: %B: where close sits inside the 20-period Bollinger band — (close − lower) / (upper − lower).
bb_pct_b.whatItMeans: Position within the volatility envelope. Above 1 is outside the upper band (stretched up), below 0 outside the lower (stretched down).

atr_pct.howComputed: Average True Range as a fraction of price: ATR(14) / close.
atr_pct.whatItMeans: Recent volatility, scaled to price. Higher means wider swings — useful for sizing stops and reading risk.

adx.howComputed: The 14-period Average Directional Index, a 0–100 measure of trend strength (direction-agnostic).
adx.whatItMeans: How strong the trend is, not which way. Above ~25 is a trending market; low values mean chop where trend signals misfire.

plus_di.howComputed: The +DI component of the 14-period directional-movement system — the strength of upward movement.
plus_di.whatItMeans: Upward directional pressure. When it leads −DI, buyers are in control.

minus_di.howComputed: The −DI component of the 14-period directional-movement system — the strength of downward movement.
minus_di.whatItMeans: Downward directional pressure. When it leads +DI, sellers are in control.

supertrend_dir.howComputed: The Supertrend direction at period 10: +1 in an uptrend, −1 in a downtrend.
supertrend_dir.whatItMeans: A discrete trend-following stance. It flips with the ATR-based trailing stop, so it lags but filters noise.

ema20_dist.howComputed: Distance of close from its 20-period EMA, as a fraction: (close − EMA20) / close.
ema20_dist.whatItMeans: How far price has stretched from its short-term mean. Large values often precede a snap-back.

ema50_dist.howComputed: Distance of close from its 50-period EMA, as a fraction: (close − EMA50) / close.
ema50_dist.whatItMeans: Stretch from the medium-term mean — a slower, more structural version of the 20-period distance.

donchian_pos.howComputed: Position of close within the 20-period Donchian channel: (close − lower) / (upper − lower).
donchian_pos.whatItMeans: Where price sits in its recent range. Near 1 is pushing recent highs (breakout territory); near 0, recent lows.

rel_volume.whatItMeans: Participation versus the recent norm. Above 1 means heavier-than-usual trade — moves on high relative volume carry more weight.

halving_phase.howComputed: Fraction of the Bitcoin halving cycle elapsed at the bar's date, in [0, 1].
halving_phase.whatItMeans: Where we are in BTC's ~4-year supply cycle — a slow macro-timing context, not a short-term signal.

days_since_halving.howComputed: Days since the most recent Bitcoin halving at the bar's UTC date.
days_since_halving.whatItMeans: Raw cycle age. Historically, distance from a halving has tracked broad phases of the BTC cycle.

mayer_multiple.whatItMeans: Price relative to its long trend. Historically stretched when high, historically cheap when low — a valuation context, not a trigger.

dist_200w_ma.howComputed: close / SMA1400 (≈200-week MA) of daily closes − 1.
dist_200w_ma.whatItMeans: Distance from the multi-year mean — a very slow cycle-valuation gauge; extremes have marked long-cycle tops and bottoms.

fng_value.howComputed: The Fear & Greed index (0–100), read lag-1 from the metric store.
fng_value.whatItMeans: Crowd sentiment. Extreme fear and extreme greed are contrarian context — associated with turns, not a guarantee of one.

fng_delta_7.howComputed: Change in the Fear & Greed value over 7 bars: fng[i] − fng[i−7] (both lag-1).
fng_delta_7.whatItMeans: How fast sentiment is swinging. Rapid shifts flag a changing mood before the level itself looks extreme.

btc_dominance.howComputed: Bitcoin's share of total crypto market cap, in percent, read lag-1.
btc_dominance.whatItMeans: Whether capital is concentrating in BTC or rotating into alts — a market-structure backdrop.

dominance_delta_7.howComputed: Change in BTC dominance over 7 bars: dominance[i] − dominance[i−7].
dominance_delta_7.whatItMeans: The direction of capital rotation. Rising dominance often accompanies risk-off within crypto.

funding_rate.howComputed: The Binance BTCUSDT perpetual funding rate, read lag-1.
funding_rate.whatItMeans: What leveraged longs pay shorts (or vice versa). Persistently high positive funding flags crowded longs — a squeeze risk.

oi_delta_7.howComputed: Fractional change in open interest over 7 bars: OI[i] / OI[i−7] − 1.
oi_delta_7.whatItMeans: Whether leverage is building or unwinding. Rising OI into a move means conviction; falling OI, position-closing.

mvrv.howComputed: The CoinMetrics BTC MVRV ratio (market value over realised value), read lag-1.
mvrv.whatItMeans: On-chain valuation — aggregate unrealised profit. Historically high at cycle tops, low at bottoms; a slow context, not timing.

ema.howComputed: Exponential Moving Average of close over the chosen period — a weighted average that reacts faster to recent bars than a simple average.
ema.whatItMeans: A smoothed trend line. Price above it leans bullish, below bearish; the shorter the period, the more closely it hugs price.

sma.howComputed: Simple Moving Average of close over the chosen period — the unweighted mean of the last N closes.
sma.whatItMeans: A smoothed trend line that weights every bar equally, so it lags more than an EMA but is steadier.

supertrend.howComputed: An ATR-based trailing-stop line (period 10, multiplier 3): it sits below price in an uptrend and above it in a downtrend, flipping when price pierces the band.
supertrend.whatItMeans: A trend-following stop-and-direction guide. The line's side of price marks the current trend; a flip marks a potential trend change.
